display.purpose: Landing hero only. Never appears in the studio.

headline.purpose: Brand-surface section heads and the loom wordmark.

title.purpose: Panel titles, inspector section heads, node titles. Heaviest thing in the studio at 13px.

body.purpose: Studio base size. Cap prose at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: 10px uppercase group labels at 0.08em tracking. The only place the system raises its voice.

code.purpose: Anything the compiler reads: types, ports, paths, keys, literals, log lines.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Nodes at rest. Lifts the card off the canvas.

shadows.name: artboard
shadows.purpose: Contact plus ambient, so an artboard reads as a sheet on a table.

shadows.name: selection-ring
shadows.purpose: Selected state, not elevation. Ink at 30%, never brand.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: State feedback only: hover, focus, selected. The studio ships none today by design.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: The only easing. No bounce, no elastic.

narrative.overview:
loomJS is a work surface before it is an application. The canvas is paper, and the things you are actually making, artboards and nodes, sit on top of it as physical objects with soft shadows underneath. Everything that is not the work is a 1px hairline and a small ink label. There is no chrome competing with the drawing.

The system is deliberately compact. Interface type runs 9px to 13px, control radii are 6px to 8px, and surface radii are 14px to 16px. This is a professional instrument for a designer who reads code, in a full working session, on a desktop or large tablet. Density is not an accident and it is not a bug to be softened. What density buys is a canvas that stays the largest thing on screen.

This system rejects the generic SaaS dashboard: rounded cards in a three-column grid, hero metrics, a sidebar of fourteen icons, uniform padding on every surface. It equally rejects the AI-product aesthetic: sparkle icons, purple-to-blue gradients, chat-first surfaces, "ask anything" bars. loomJS emits deterministic code; nothing in the interface may imply the output was guessed.
keyCharacteristics: Paper canvas, floating work, hairline everything else
9px to 13px interface type; mono for every value, type, and identifier
Flat at rest; a shadow means the thing genuinely floats
Tablet and up, flex-first, with a graceful guard below 768px

rules.name: The Signal Reserve Rule
rules.body: The six signal colors are spent only on their assigned meaning: brand red on the primary action and FN, each category hue on its category. A category hue used on a toolbar, a badge, a hover state, or an illustration corrupts the graph's type system and is prohibited.

rules.name: The Ink Furniture Rule
rules.body: Selection, focus, active tabs, and hover chrome are ink. The studio never highlights its own furniture in brand red, because the designer must be able to find the one red thing that is an action.

rules.name: The Never-Only-Color Rule
rules.body: A category hue never travels alone. Every node, port, and chip that uses a category color also carries its label or a distinguishing shape, so a colorblind user reads the graph exactly as fast. Color IS the type system at a glance.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: If the compiler reads it, it is set in JetBrains Mono. Type names, port names, env keys, table and column names, file paths, and any literal value. If a human wrote it to be read by a human, it is Archivo.

rules.name: The Ten-Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: 10px uppercase labels and 9px metadata are the smallest permitted steps. Nothing smaller ships, and nothing at those sizes is ever the only carrier of a piece of information.

rules.name: The Readable Grey Rule
rules.body: Any text on panel or canvas is ink-2 (#4B5058, 7.8:1) or darker. ink-3 (#868D97) fails AA as text and is reserved for rules, dots and other non-text marks. On the brand surface's ink fold, the muted step (#9AA1AA) clears 6.6:1 and is safe.

rules.name: The Floating Claim Rule
rules.body: A shadow says "this floats." Panels do not float, rows do not float, cards in a list do not float. If it is attached to the layout, it gets a hairline and no shadow.

rules.name: The Flat Depth Test
rules.body: If two surfaces sit at the same z-height and you can tell them apart only by shadow, the shadow is wrong. Separate them with a hairline or with the canvas / panel fill pair instead.

dos: Do reserve #EC3013 for the single primary action and the FN node category, and spend it once per screen at most.
Do make selection, focus, and active chrome ink (#1B1D21), so the one red thing on screen is always an action.
Do pair every category hue with its label or a distinguishing shape, every time.
Do draw structure with 1px #E8EAEE hairlines. Reach for the hairline before the shadow.
Do set anything the compiler reads (types, ports, paths, keys, values) in JetBrains Mono.
Do give every interactive element a visible :focus-visible state and a keyboard path, including canvas, inspector, and node graph.
Do vary padding by role: 10px in panels, 6px 10px in node heads, 4px 10px in controls, 4px 6px in inputs. Uniform padding across every surface is the SaaS dashboard tell.
Do keep body prose to 65 to 75ch on the rare surfaces that have prose.
Do set text on light surfaces in ink-2 or darker. ink-3 is a mark colour, not a text colour.
donts: Don't build a generic SaaS dashboard: no rounded cards in a three-column grid, no hero metric block, no icon-stack sidebar, no identical repeating card layouts.
Don't reach for the AI-product aesthetic: no sparkle icons, no purple-to-blue gradients, no chat-first surface, no "ask anything" bar.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, rows, callouts, or log lines.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Emphasis is weight and size.
Don't use glassmorphism or backdrop blur in the studio. The floating nav on the landing surface is the one deliberate exception and it does not transfer.
Don't add a dark theme or a theme toggle. Light mode only (guardrail 21).
Don't spend a category hue on chrome, decoration, illustration, or a hover state.
Don't introduce a new hue, a new radius step, or a new font. The palette, the radius scale, and the Archivo plus JetBrains Mono pairing are fixed by guardrails 19 to 24.
Don't use pure #000 or a pure black shadow. Shadows are tinted rgb(20 22 26 / …).
Don't reach for a modal. Exhaust inline and progressive alternatives first; a modal is a failure of the "never left the canvas" principle.
Don't animate layout properties, and never animate anything during a canvas drag.
